title: Spectral sparsity avoids its parameter
statement: Let $n,s\in\mathbb N$, and let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\{\pm1\}$. Suppose $1<s$ and $1<s\bigl(2(1/2)^{\lfloor\log_2 s\rfloor}\bigr)^2$, where $\lfloor\log_2 s\rfloor$ denotes the integer logarithm used to define the granularity. Then the number of nonzero vector Fourier coefficients of $x\mapsto f(x)$ is not $s$.
